races.name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Alpha Legend
runners_data.comment: £24,000 yearling; has plenty of stamina in pedigree and could be a longer-term prospect
runners_data.spotlight: 32,000euros foal, £24,000 yearling; first foal; dam unraced sister to winners Rhythmic Intent (useful 1m2f-14.5f) and Fortune Triple (HK 1m1f/1m3f), is granddaughter of French Oaks winner Caerlina; has plenty of stamina on dam's side and he could be a longer-term prospect.

runners_data.name: Parading
runners_data.comment: Has speed and stamina in pedigree and interesting to see how he figures in market
runners_data.spotlight: Ardad colt; third foal; dam 9.4f/1m2f winner (including 2yo; RPR 87), half-sister to 1m Listed winner Staying On, out of maiden half-sister to Rockfel winner Yawl, family of Oaks winner Talent; has speed and stamina in pedigree and interesting to see how he figures in market.

runners_data.name: Sky Secret
runners_data.comment: Has speedy pedigree and she needs a close look for yard that that won this race last year
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; 15,000gns foal, 42,000euros yearling; fifth foal; half-brother to 6f AW winner Black Cab (RPR 56); dam 6f winner (86), sister to 5f/6f Group 3 winner Swiss Diva, half-sister to 5f Group 3 winner Swiss Spirit, out of 5f Listed winner; has lots of speed in pedigree and she's an interesting newcomer for yard that that won this race last year.

runners_data.name: Donegal Rose
runners_data.comment: £44,000 yearling; yard 2-3 with 2yos this season and she needs a close look on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 35,000euros foal, £44,000 yearling; Kodiac filly who is closely related to 7f AW 2yo winner Dynamite Katie (RPR 78); dam unraced half-sister to French 1m4f Listed winner Balaythous and useful 7f-1m1f winner Saphirside; yard 2-3 with 2yos this season and she needs a close look on debut.

runners_data.name: Allaboutthelunch
runners_data.comment: 4,000gns yearling; could be one for later on and he's probably best watched on debut
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; 30,000gns foal, 4,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Bill Silvers (7f; RPR 99) and Gaelic Approach (1m4f; 77); dam placed 1m-1m4f (78), half-sister to 1m4f winners Empyrea and La Joya; could be one for later on and he's probably best watched on debut.

runners_data.name: Indian Land
runners_data.comment: Yard 20% with 2yos last season and he needs a close look on debut
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; Land Force half-brother to winners Tribal Craft (1m2f-1m6f including Group 3; RPR 110), Seattle King (7f 2yo/1m2f; 90), Star Maker (11.6f Flat, 81; 2m-2m3f hurdle) and Dream Seeker (German 6.5f); dam 1m/1m2f winner (93); yard has had a 2yo winner this season and had a 20% record with juveniles last term.

runners_data.name: Top Cote
runners_data.comment: 15,000gns yearling; others look more likely and he's probably best watched on debut
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; 7,000euros foal, 15,000euros yearling; first foal of a 7f 2yo winner (RPR 97), out of French 10.5f winning half-sister to 1m1f Flat and 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase winner Authentic Act; others look more likely and he's best watched unless market suggests otherwise.

runners_data.name: Turnstile
runners_data.comment: Showed ability behind a useful prospect at Thirsk; key player if he can build on that
runners_data.spotlight: Ran green and hung left from halfway but he was only just run out of third on his debut at Thirsk (good) two weeks ago; that was an encouraging start behind a useful prospect and he's a key player if he can build on that.

runners_data.name: Postcard
runners_data.comment: 16-1 at Bath three weeks ago and she finished a remote eighth of ten
runners_data.spotlight: 1,000gns yearling; 16-1 at Bath (good) three weeks ago and she dropped out before before finishing a remote eighth of ten.

runners_data.name: Everatease
runners_data.comment: Big market drifter at Wolverhampton and he finished a remote sixth of seven
runners_data.spotlight: Big market drifter at Wolverhampton (AW; 11-1) two weeks ago and he finished into a remote sixth of seven; should be more streetwise this time but he needs a transformation on his second start.

runners_data.name: Mr Macartney
runners_data.comment: Well backed into 3-1 at Wolverhampton but he never got involved; needs improvement
runners_data.spotlight: 10,000gns February foal; well backed into 3-1 at Wolverhampton (AW) two weeks ago but he never got involved before finishing a well-held fourth of seven; should benefit from that experience but he needs plenty of progress on this switch to turf.

runners_data.name: From Me To You
runners_data.comment: Didn't live up to market expectations at Newbury but he should know much more this time
runners_data.spotlight: January foal; £55,000 yearling; didn't live up to market expectations when seventh on Newbury debut (good; 7-2) last week but he ran green after a slow start; should know much more this time and it wouldn't be a surprise if he took a major step forward.

races.name: Caffreys Black Stout King Richard III Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Ten Pounds
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning after 99 days off, lacks tongue-tie from last run
runners_data.comment: Record of 5-12 but he was down the field at Newcastle last time; needs more after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 5-10 for Harry Charlton and his last win was in a conditions event at Kempton (6f, AW) in October; ran without his declared tongue-tie when fourth on stable debut at Southwell in January but he finished down the field in another Class 2 handicap at Newcastle two weeks later; conditions should be fine on this return to turf but he needs to step up again after another break.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid AW form, trainer David O'Meara in decent nick at 5/28
runners_data.comment: C&D winner who scored on AW in November but he needs more progress to defy this mark
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner who ended his 2025 campaign with a success and creditable effort over 5f at Newcastle (AW); was as good as ever in those two runs but he was well below form on his reappearance at Pontefract (5f, good to soft) 18 days ago; may have needed that run but he needs more progress to defy this mark.

runners_data.name: Annaf
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won Group 3 at Ascot last season, strong finishing kick suits race shape
runners_data.comment: Group 3 winner over 6f last autumn and he has possibilities back in a handicap
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season with a game win in Group 3 at Ascot (6f, soft) in October; repeatedly met trouble when only seventh in Saudi Arabia (a race he'd won two years earlier) in February and things didn't really go his way again in a Listed race at Doncaster last month; has possibilities on this drop back in class and his last handicap win was off 1lb higher.

runners_data.name: Fast Track Harry
runners_data.note: Prominent style with recent AW success, wearing tongue-tie and only 28 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Held in hat-trick bid at Kempton but he still has potential and is not ruled back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Dual turf winner who made it 2-2 on AW when completing a double at Newcastle (6f; off 4lb lower) last month; didn't fire in his hat-trick bid at Kempton but he still has potential and is not ruled out in suitable conditions back on turf.

runners_data.name: Russet Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 204 days for new trainer Kevin Ryan, undergone wind surgery
runners_data.comment: Returns after wind surgery but has mixed record when fresh and his last win was in 2023
runners_data.spotlight: Two 5f wins for Roger Varian but latest was in June 2023 and he was quiet last season; returns for new yard after wind surgery but he has a mixed record when fresh and this is highly competitive; down the list.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Whisper
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, went close off this mark at Southwell recently, 22 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Placed off this mark at Newcastle latest and he's still unexposed on turf; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Completed an AW hat-trick when scoring on his handicap debut at Newcastle (6f) last April; held in six subsequent runs but he went close off this mark at Southwell in November and was a creditable third at Newcastle three weeks ago; now returns to turf but he ran well in a fast-ground Listed event last spring and he's still unexposed in this sphere; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse now with Robert Cowell, needs to find extra spark but proven at this level
runners_data.comment: Fair efforts in two runs for new yard and he could be dangerous back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Listed winner (5f/6f) for his previous yards and he's run respectably in two 5f handicaps for his new trainer this spring; needs to find some extra spark but he's edging down the weights and this step back up in trip looks a good move.

runners_data.name: Strike Red
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran with good recent third at Newcastle, apprentice Warren Fentiman takes 3lb off
runners_data.comment: Second in Stewards' Cup last summer and runner-up at Newcastle 12 days ago; respected
runners_data.spotlight: On lengthy losing but he's a smart handicapper on his day and he returned from five months off with a good third at Newcastle (6f, AW) two weeks ago; should benefit from that run and he remains well treated on his second in the Stewards' Cup last August; interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Prince Of India
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won four times last year, wearing tongue-tie and fresh from 9 days ago
runners_data.comment: Four wins last year but his progress seems to have flattened out; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Won four times during a progressive campaign last year but he's come up short in Listed/Group 3 events this spring; seems ideally suited by fast ground but he's still 4lb higher than for his last win and has some work to do back in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse better on AW, 7lb claimer Harry Vigors reduces weight significantly
runners_data.comment: 1-26 on turf but he's been in good form on AW and he's on lower mark back in this sphere
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time AW winner who has finished close up on Tapeta (5f/6f) in his last three runs; record of 1-26 on turf but he's on a lower mark in this sphere and he ran well in the Great St Wilfrid at Ripon (6f, good to firm) last summer; dangerous.

runners_data.name: Roman Dragon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from Bahrain spell, unpredictable but capable on his day
runners_data.comment: Chester specialist who is not easy to predict and others are preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Well handicapped on his best form last season but he's not easy to predict and has been up and down during another spell in Bahrain since December; comes with risks attached back in Britain and most of his wins have been at Chester; tongue-tie worn last time is removed.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Chief
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 98 days off, consistent performer who handles good ground
runners_data.comment: Reliable type who is very effective on fast ground and he's respected back from a break
runners_data.spotlight: Ran creditably at Lingfield in January when bidding for a 6f AW double; 8lb higher than when second at Newmarket (7f) on last turf attempt but he's proved consistent since being gelded and his first two handicap wins were on good to firm; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Betsen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent Tapeta form, this represents step back up in class
runners_data.comment: In good form on AW but this is a step back up in grade and his sole turf win was in 2024
runners_data.spotlight: Won on stable debut at Southwell (6f, Tapeta) in November and he's posted some solid efforts since then; hard to rule out another good run but this is a step back up in grade and sole turf win was 19 months ago.

races.paceDynamic: Ten Pounds and Dark Cloud Rising will contest the early lead from their prominent styles, with Zoulu Chief also likely to track closely. The pace should be honest but not destructive over 6f at Leicester, allowing the large contingent of hold-up horses to get into contention. With 9 of 13 runners employing hold-up tactics, there's significant closing speed in reserve. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish well, as the modest early pace will leave plenty in the tank for a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves steady as expected with limited pressure on the leaders
scenarios.body: The large hold-up contingent will have energy preserved for a telling finish, overwhelming the early leaders in the final furlong. Horses with proven finishing kicks will thrive in this tactical battle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Steal
scenarios.trigger: If Ten Pounds and Dark Cloud Rising collaborate to set a measured tempo without serious challenge
scenarios.body: One of the early leaders can maintain their advantage as the hold-up horses leave their runs too late on good ground. The lack of early pressure allows a front-runner to stay strong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes stronger than anticipated with multiple horses vying for position
scenarios.body: The increased tempo will compromise both leaders and hold-up horses, favouring those who can adapt tactically from midfield positions. Horses with versatile running styles gain the advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes crawling slow in the middle stages creating a dash from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test where horses with natural acceleration excel regardless of early position. Raw pace trumps tactical positioning in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Ten Pounds setting the pace after 99 days off - fitness levels crucial for stamina in closing stages
Strike Red and Prince Of India both proven finishers who could benefit massively from steady early gallop
Fast Track Harry wearing tongue-tie again after recent AW success - prominent position could prove decisive
The large hold-up contingent of 9 horses creating potential traffic problems in final 2f
Apprentice riders on Strike Red (3lb off) and Fivethousandtoone (7lb off) reducing weight significantly

races.name: Rekorderlig Premium Fruit Cider Handicap

runners_data.name: Dashing Dick
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner returning after 175 days off with previous good to firm concerns but won his last start
runners_data.comment: Won at Newmarket (good to soft) in November; well beaten in this race on return last year
runners_data.spotlight: Said goodbye to 2025 with a Newmarket win (6f, good to soft) in November; has won on good to firm but he missed a recent intended return on the surface and this might be needed anyway (soundly beaten here last April).

runners_data.name: Mr Lightside
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can lead, sliding down handicap but disappointing in recent turf handicaps for Michael Appleby
runners_data.comment: Smart 2yo; humdrum form in three turf handicaps, way back at Bath last week
runners_data.spotlight: Can lead; smart 2yo who began 3yo season on a mark of 102; has shown just humdrum form in three turf handicaps, despite a sliding mark, and was way back behind Justcallmepete at Bath last week; has it to prove now.

runners_data.name: Under The Twilight
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare better for Doncaster reappearance, back to winning mark from Windsor success on good to firm
runners_data.comment: Back on the same mark as Windsor win (6f, good to firm) last June; first run on this track
runners_data.spotlight: Should be all the better for her Doncaster reappearance and she's back on the same mark as for her Windsor success (6f, good to firm) last June; however, all her turf wins have come there and at Salisbury and this is the first time she's run on this track.

runners_data.name: Ormolulu
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after long break but weighted to go well on best form with good to firm track record
runners_data.comment: 1-1 over C&D; lacks recent run but weighted to go well on best 6f form on good to firm
runners_data.spotlight: Weighted to go well on best turf form and the drying ground shouldn't cause her any grief, having run so well on good to firm at York (6f) last June; also a winner of her one C&D start, in 2023, and the booking of Billy Loughnane signals intent; has prospects despite lacking a recent run.

runners_data.name: Justcallmepete
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with better AW record but won impressively at Bath last week and has useful 6f grass form
runners_data.comment: Clear winner at Bath (extended 5f) last week; 6lb higher but this mark is not beyond him
runners_data.spotlight: Has a better strike-rate on AW than turf but he's capable of useful 6f form on grass and made short work of his rivals at Bath (extended 5f, good) last week; now 6lb higher but this mark isn't beyond him on past exploits; would have welcomed rain but still considered.

runners_data.name: Dapper Valley
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for in-form James Owen stable, mixed recent form but capable at this level on his day
runners_data.comment: Well treated when winning 3 of last 4 on AW/turf (6f) in 2025; good turf run in UAE latest
runners_data.spotlight: Had ups and downs since showing decent form earlier in career and was well treated when starting out for this trainer in 2025, winning three of his last four 6f starts on AW and turf; went down only narrowly back on turf (good to firm; headgear left off) in UAE during March and he's of interest now back with former yard.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with perfect C&D record, won pulling clear here 12 days ago and handles good ground
runners_data.comment: 2-2 over C&D, pulling well clear 12 days ago (good); needs to defy a 9lb rise
runners_data.spotlight: Winner of both C&D starts, in October (good to soft) and when pulling well clear (good) 12 days ago; has won on good to firm so the warm weather shouldn't be a problem but the new 9lb higher mark might be.

races.paceDynamic: Dashing Dick and Mr Lightside will contest early pace with Dapper Valley likely to track closely behind, creating a genuine tempo over 6f at Leicester. The prominent runners will set a solid gallop but nothing excessive given the small field size. This pace setup creates opportunities for the hold-up horses to close late down the straight. The race shape favours horses with finishing kick ability who can position themselves midfield and unleash late speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Late closers dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuine enough to soften up the leaders
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses Under The Twilight, Ormolulu and Wreck It Ryley get perfect positioning to unleash finishing kicks in the final furlong. The prominent runners pay for their exertions as the closers sweep past.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runners stay there
scenarios.trigger: If Dashing Dick and Mr Lightside can dictate fractions without going too hard early
scenarios.body: The pace becomes controlled enough for the leaders to kick clear in the final two furlongs before the hold-up horses can get organised. Dapper Valley benefits from tracking the moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Justcallmepete surges through
scenarios.trigger: If the Bath winner gets the perfect setup with leaders going steady then quickening
scenarios.body: His recent winning form and tactical speed allows him to find gaps and strike decisively when the race develops. The combination of fitness and class tells in a driving finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If the small field and lack of natural pace forces mean no one wants to go forward
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy tactical affair with stop-start fractions that suit nothing. Whoever gets first run from the back of the field benefits most from the sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Dashing Dick may not handle the faster ground despite returning to winning form last time
Mr Lightside's recent turf handicap form suggests he may struggle despite sliding mark
Under The Twilight should strip fitter after her Doncaster reappearance run
Wreck It Ryley has perfect course form with two wins from two Leicester starts
Ormolulu faces fitness test after 173-day absence despite being well treated by handicapper

races.name: Alpacalypse Session IPA Handicap

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits this race shape, Harry Davies capable, good course form but question over this sharper track
runners_data.comment: Close 2nd on AW return; well held since but chance on strong-finishing 3rd here last year
runners_data.spotlight: Both turf wins on Brighton's sharp track but she made up plenty of ground when a never-nearer third in this race (good) last year and it wouldn't surprise to see her return to form after a low-key Southwell run last time, having gone close there on her reappearance the time before.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, 59-day break concerning, Laura Coughlan's 3lb claim helps, shown ability on AW
runners_data.comment: 0-15 but had two close calls over 6f on AW this year; acts on turf and may well figure
runners_data.spotlight: Not yet off the mark but she's had two close calls on the AW this year, notably when only just failing to get up at Wolverhampton (6f) in February, against one on the fifth leg of a seven-timer; acts on turf, too, and may well figure back from short break.

runners_data.name: Profiteer
runners_data.comment: Three wins in 2024; mostly underpowered in 2025 but now 10lb lower than last April
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins in 2024, at 7f and 5f; mostly rather underpowered in 2025 and no obvious sign fitting headgear was a help in the autumn, but he's 10lb lower than on reappearance last April so there is handicapping hope.

runners_data.name: Dragon God
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner prone to fading, slow starter adds complications, 20 days since last run ideal
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced maiden; not disgraced over 5f latest; down 3lb; can do better back at 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden for two yards but he didn't get the best of runs after a slow start at Bath (first 5f run; good) and may well be ready to play more of a part now back at 6f following a further 3lb drop.

runners_data.name: Shark Two One
runners_data.note: Prominent runner, 199-day absence major concern despite past excuses, Jack Dace's 5lb claim valuable
runners_data.comment: Likes it here and last 2 wins on this track (7f); needs more on usual reappearance efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Five turf wins at 6f-7f, the latest two over the latter trip on this track; he's had some excuses for low-key reappearances in the past but it's still a stretch to expect him to be on song for this one.

runners_data.name: Call Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, recent AW form decent, long absence from turf but fresh off 10-day break
runners_data.comment: Two AW wins in 2026; long time since he's run well on turf but not out of it on past form
runners_data.spotlight: Two AW wins in January, over 6f and 7f; just averagely handicapped now and it's a long time since he's run well on turf but he wouldn't be out of it on past form on grass.

runners_data.name: Instant Bond
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner, tongue-tie fitted, AW winner in March but turf form moderate recently
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in 2 turf handicaps in 2025; broke duck on AW in March; may do better on grass
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in two turf handicaps either side of a break in 2025 but he was off the mark on the AW in March and has run respectably in defeat since; might well have more to offer on this surface.

runners_data.name: Just King High
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but fades late, blinkers and tongue-tie applied, 14 days since last run perfect
runners_data.comment: Won 2yo AW maiden; tough in 2025; found some form on AW in March; held latest for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Won 2yo AW maiden; his 3yo season never really got going but he was on a much-reduced mark when runner-up on two occasions (7f) in March; well held on yard debut since, though, and likely best watched back on turf.

runners_data.name: Von Krolock
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner, visor fitted, recent AW winner with good course form, Christian Howarth's 3lb claim

runners_data.name: Mickey Mongoose
runners_data.note: Prominent style, blowpipe headgear, prefers longer trips but has shown 7f ability recently
runners_data.comment: Sole turf win at 1m2f; three AW wins at 1m/7f; in form but having first 6f run since debut
runners_data.spotlight: Sole turf win came over 1m2f in 2023 and three subsequent successes have been on the AW (1m and 7f); has continued to run well since the latest of them in February but this is his first 6f run since his debut.

runners_data.name: Cameley Days
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter with fading tendency, 171-day break concerning, needs to find turf form again
runners_data.comment: Two sprint wins (good to soft and heavy) for new yard in the autumn; can find more
runners_data.spotlight: Well held on AW in November but progressive on turf for new yard previously, following a close second at Yarmouth (6f, good) with wins there (good to soft) and at Bath (extended 5f, heavy); may well do better on good to firm as her dam's best form for this yard came on the same going.

races.paceDynamic: Cameley Days is the lone confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, likely getting an uncontested lead in this 6f handicap. With most of the field showing hold-up tendencies (Dark Sun, Dragon God, Call Glory, Instant Bond, Just King High, Von Krolock), there's minimal early pace pressure, allowing for a sustainable tempo through the early stages. The race will develop into a typical sprint finish with the hold-up brigade trying to sweep up the pace-setter in the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can position close enough to strike, as the lack of early pace will create a bunched finish where being too far back becomes problematic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Cameley Days gets soft fractions and isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: The pace-setter maintains enough in reserve to resist late challengers, with the hold-up horses leaving their runs too late from the pedestrian pace. Prominent runners like Starsong and Mickey Mongoose find better positions to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and hold-up horses get clear runs
scenarios.body: The bunched finish allows patient riders to time their challenges perfectly, with Von Krolock and Dark Sun benefiting from their tactical positioning. Hold-up specialists capitalize on the sustained gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Pressure Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Shark Two One or Mickey Mongoose press Cameley Days early
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field more than expected, favoring horses with natural speed and prominent running styles. Starsong's tactical pace and finishing kick prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Problems Decide
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches significantly and several runners get hampered
scenarios.body: Clear runs become premium and whichever hold-up horses avoid interference benefit most, while prominent racers suffer from the scrimmaging. Jockey skills and luck determine the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Cameley Days could steal this if getting uncontested fractions - monitor early sectionals for sustainable pace
Traffic problems likely in straight with 9+ hold-up horses converging - watch for clear runs and interference
Dark Sun returning after 59 days with claiming rider - fitness and ring rustiness could be decisive factors
Starsong's finishing kick from prominent position could be key if pace becomes truly run affair
Von Krolock's recent AW form translating to turf - headgear change and course experience notable

runners_data.name: Act Of Generosity
runners_data.comment: 875,000gns yearling; striking newcomer and he holds a Derby entry
runners_data.spotlight: 875,000gns yearling; first foal; dam Listed-placed 1m/8.5f winner (RPR 98), half-sister to winners Bite Of The Cherry (useful 1m5f), Pietra Dura (7f 2yo) and Ever Rigg (1m4f; dam of 1m2f-1m4f Group 1 winner Postponed), out of Moyglare Stud/Lowther winner; interesting newcomer and he holds Derby entry.

runners_data.name: Yafreh
runners_data.comment: Brother to smart 7f-1m2f winner Al Mubhir; needs checking in market on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth foal; brother to 7f-1m2f winner Al Mubhir (including Listed; RPR 115), half-brother to three winners including Yabher (1m-1m4f; 96); dam 7f-1m1f winner (including Group 3; 112); has good standard to aim at on debut but he needs checking in market.

runners_data.name: Heyzoom
runners_data.comment: Sets standard on his debut third at Wolverhampton and he's open to progress upped in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Brother to 1m/8.5f winner Rowayeh (RPR 94), closely related to 8.6f AW 2yo/1m2f turf Listed winner Falakeyah (106); held in third when odds-on at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in November but he finished well behind two rivals who were ridden more prominently; sets a good standard on that promising effort and he's open to progress upped in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Porter's Song will lead uncontested from the front, setting a sustainable gallop that won't stretch the field early. With most of the field carrying hold-up or midfield styles (Yokkell, Blackwater Lilly, Not So Sobers, Happy Chandler, Silkies Sib, Beauty Generation, He's Our Cracker, Shifra), there's minimal early pressure on the leader. The pace will gradually build from the 3f marker as the large pack of hold-up horses fan out seeking racing room. This setup strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can position close enough to avoid traffic problems, while making life difficult for pure hold-up horses relying on late kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Porter's Song maintains steady fractions without serious challenge until 2f out
scenarios.body: The lone leader gets first run while the hold-up brigade gets caught in traffic behind the wall of closers. Evelyn's Phoenix and Miss Chester can track the pace without being asked for effort too early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Nightmare
scenarios.trigger: If the large group of hold-up horses get bunched and struggle for clear running in the straight
scenarios.body: Prominent racers avoid the melee while hold-up horses like Yokkell and Beauty Generation find trouble. Happy Chandler gets a perfect tow just behind the leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Porter's Song goes too slow early and multiple horses improve position before halfway
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where class and recent form matter most. Evelyn's Phoenix's Saturday win form and Happy Chandler's Bath second make them dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Chester or Evelyn's Phoenix challenge Porter's Song for the early lead
scenarios.body: Strong gallop suits stamina types and horses proven at the trip. Yokkell's class and Silkies Sib's 1m2f win credentials come to the fore late.

watchPoints.text: Porter's Song could get uncontested lead and prove hard to peg back if allowed easy fractions
Traffic problems likely in straight with 10+ hold-up horses needing room simultaneously
Miss Chester and Shifra both show fade patterns that could worsen in big competitive field
Evelyn's Phoenix quick turnaround from Saturday win tests recovery but trainer form solid
Happy Chandler's reduced mark and Bath form revival makes him value at bigger prices

races.paceDynamic: Great Success and Venetian Romance will likely lead early with Eduardo Calderon and Chelio also showing pace, creating a moderate gallop over this 7f trip. The prominent runners should get an easy time of it with no confirmed tearaway leaders in the field. Lion Of Mali, Pretty Danielle, Horwich and Circle Of Trust will be held up looking for gaps in the straight. This pace setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as the early pace will be steady enough to allow closers to get into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate as expected with no fierce speed duel
scenarios.body: The closers get the perfect setup to unleash finishing kicks from off the pace. Lion Of Mali and Pretty Danielle are best positioned to capitalize with their proven ability to finish strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Great Success or Venetian Romance find easy early fractions and kick clear
scenarios.body: One of the pace-setters gets first run on the field and proves too strong for the closers. Their early position advantage becomes decisive in a race where the kick-back is limited.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: A horse positioned just off the leaders gets the perfect trip tracking the pace. Chelio or Eduardo Calderon can bridge the gap between pace-setters and closers to strike at the optimal moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Great Success and Venetian Romance go too fast early and fall apart
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair where any horse with a clean run can prevail. The form book goes out the window as tired leaders create opportunities for any runner with late momentum.

watchPoints.text: Great Success and Venetian Romance must be watched for early fractions - if they go too fast the race will fall apart
Lion Of Mali needs a clean passage from his hold-up position as he's been narrowly beaten recently
Pretty Danielle should be prominent in betting after her encouraging return from a break last time
Circle Of Trust is having his first run for 221 days and may need the outing despite his 7f form
Eduardo Calderon is making his handicap debut after a long break and could be well treated
